thread:
sarah: Quick async — we need to finalize the metric defs for the new performance dashboard before Monday. Specifically TTFT, tok/s, and p95. Can people confirm current canonical definitions and any caveats? @kai @mikhail :eyes:

kai: short answer: TTFT = time from request ingress to first token emitted by the runtime (server side). Important: exclude client-side network and parsing. We currently instrument both server_ingest_ts and first_token_emit_ts.

mikhail: +1. Caveat: for cached prefixes we sometimes see very low TTFT which skews median. For dashboard I recommend using p50/p95 of requests that had cold KV cache (label cache="cold").

liz: for tok/s we report tokens_emitted / inference_duration_seconds (server runtime time). Note this differs from raw model throughput (model-only) because we include decoding and post-processing. Should we add a separate "model_tok_s" metric?

anand: yes please. Add model_tok_s (only model exec time excluding decode) so teams can separate infra vs decode perf. Also, define precise label set: model, seq_len, batch_size, quantization, region.

sarah: agreed on separate model_tok_s. For p95: do we want end-to-end p95 (client->client) or server p95? My vote: server p95 as primary, with end-to-end as secondary.

kai: +1. Server p95 is actionable. End-to-end includes network jitter and client lib differences. Keep both but alert on server p95 only.

mikhail: proposed Grafana/PromQL snippets — feel free to copy:
```
# TTFT p95 (server side, exclude warm cache)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(ttft_seconds_bucket{cache="cold"}[5m])) by (le, model))

# tokens/sec (model only)
rate(model_tokens_emitted_total[1m]) / avg_over_time(model_exec_seconds[1m])
```

liz: nit: model_exec_seconds should be a histogram or counter-derived rate. Might be easier to compute tok/s as sum(rate(model_tokens_total[1m])) by (model) / sum(rate(model_exec_seconds_sum[1m])) by (model) if using prometheus histograms.

perf-bot: nightly-perf-check completed: baseline vs main — p95_server latency regressed by +12% on model rtd-4q-1.2. See /perf/reports/2026-03-15-rt4q.json :warning:

anand: thanks bot. @mikhail can you pick up profiling for rtd-4q? Might be quantization interaction. If it's model-only, we can roll back.

mikhail: will profile this afternoon. Quick ask for instrumentation: please ensure request labels include rollout_tag and cache state (warm|cold). Otherwise it's hard to slice.

sarah: action items I captured:
- kai: validate TTFT instrumentation + add server/client tagging (due EOD)
- liz: add model_tok_s metric and make dashboard panel for model vs runtime tok/s (due tomorrow)
- mikhail: profile rtd-4q p95 regression and report findings (due EOD tomorrow)
- anand: draft alert thresholds (suggest p95_server > 1.5s for critical, TTFT p95 > 0.3s for warn)

kai: i pushed a tiny PR that tags ingress vs client in trace spans. pinged @sarah for review.

liz: starting dashboard draft now. will post screenshot in this thread when ready.

anand: alert proposal: warn if p95_server > 300ms AND tok/s drops > 20% vs baseline for 5m; critical if p95_server > 1500ms OR error_rate > 1%. open to numbers.

sarah: sounds reasonable. let's iterate. If anyone needs me to unblock dashboards access or workspace folders shout here. :thumbsup:

kai: review done, comments left.

mikhail: profile run queued, attaching flamegraph link when done.

liz: screenshot uploaded -> /dashboards/drafts/rt-perf-2026-03-15.png :eyes:

sarah: awesome. We'll do a quick sync if the regression looks real. Otherwise we'll just tweak thresholds and roll. Thanks all! :tada:
